title: Review threads
description: One markdown thread of notes per checkout, where the user, the workers in it and its reviewers talk about its unlanded work.

guidance.brief: Review threads: get your work reviewed, read and answer notes. `tower x reviews thread` reads yours, `tower x reviews review <CALLSIGN> --tell` hires a reviewer.
guidance.full:
Every checkout has one review thread: your worktree, or `main` for the main checkouts. The user, the checkout's workers and reviewers append notes about work that hasn't landed, often quoting lines.

Use it when your task asks for a review or the user says "get yourself reviewed", when told of new notes, or when you want a note on your own work for the next reader of the diff: a non-obvious choice, a risk, something left undone. Not a place for write-ups, and not for work that has landed.

- `tower x reviews review <CALLSIGN> --tell`: hires a reviewer in a fork of that worker's checkout, uncommitted work included. It reviews once and leaves notes; `--tell` also sends them to the worker. To get yourself reviewed, first leave a note stating the goal and what was agreed, then name your own callsign. A review is never limited by the floor's hiring limits.
- `tower x reviews thread [checkout]`: the thread of your checkout (a reviewer's: its author's), then the notes new to you and the repo names its anchors take.
- `tower x reviews note [--on <checkout>] [--re <k>] [--at <repo>:<path>:<from>-<to> …] <<'EOF'` … `EOF`: appends a note under your callsign, the body on stdin. `--re 3` or `--re n3` answers n3. Each `--at` anchors it to lines, quoted from your checkout as they are now.
- `tower x reviews resolve <k> … [--on <checkout>]`: marks those notes resolved with a note of its own; anything on stdin is said under the mark. Resolve a note once it is dealt with: the fix landed, or its author agreed it stays.
- `tower x reviews send <CALLSIGN>`: submits into that worker a pointer to the notes new to it.

When told of new notes: read the thread, act on each (change the code, or decide it stays), and answer each with `--re`: what you changed, with the commit, or why it stays. Then, when a worker hired you, report to it: what changed and whether the work is ready. The thread alone is no report: your hirer isn't watching it. Only these words write the thread: never edit its file.

The checkout its review thread is about: a reviewer's is its author's.

threadState.description: Where the work its thread is about stands, with the thread Tidy filed once it landed.

unseen.description: The notes on its thread it hasn't seen (after its own last one), while its thread's work is live.

filed.description: The thread Tidy filed once the work in its own checkout landed.

of.description: The callsign of the worker whose work this one reviews.

note.description: The call that adds a note to its thread while that work is live: the renderer adds the author and what the note says.

resolved.description: Its resolved notes, by number, in order.

checkout.description: A worktree's name, or `main` for the main checkouts.

author.description: Who writes: the user's name (`board.user.name`), or a worker's callsign.

re.description: The number of the message this one answers.

anchors.description: The lines the note is about, each quoted as it was.

repo.description: The repo as the Changes pane names it: its main checkout's folder.

append.description: Append a message to the checkout's review thread, made on the first one; it is numbered one past the last.

words.label: Note
words.hint: add a note to the checkout's review thread

checkout.description: A worktree's name, or `main` for the main checkouts. Left out, the caller's: a reviewer's is its author's.

author.description: Who writes: the user's name (`board.user.name`), or a worker's callsign. Left out, the calling worker's.

notes.description: The notes it resolves, by number: each one of the thread's, unresolved and no resolution itself.

body.description: What the resolver adds under the mark.

on.description: The checkout, by the name `note` gives it: `checkout` as a word's flag. Left out, the caller's: a reviewer's is its author's.

resolves.description: The notes it resolves as they are typed, `3` or `n3`, for a caller that gives no `notes`.

resolve.description: Mark notes of the checkout's thread resolved by appending a note, numbered like any other, whose body opens `**Resolved:** n3, n4`: append-only, and read as a plain note wherever resolving is unknown.

words.label: Resolve
words.hint: mark the note resolved on its thread

of.description: The callsign of the worker whose work is reviewed, looked for on `project`, then on every floor: the reviewer starts on that worker's.

by.description: The session hiring the reviewer: its hire is logged in its log, and never limited.

tell.description: The reviewer sends a pointer to its notes to the author when done.

hire.description: Hire a reviewer of a worker's unlanded work: a worker in a fork of its checkout, uncommitted work included, that reviews once against its goal and leaves notes on its thread. It sits beside its author, in its crew, and is exempt from hiring limits.

words.label: Review
words.hint: hire a reviewer in a fork of this worker's checkout

on.description: The checkout whose thread it goes on. Left out, the caller's: a reviewer's is its author's.

at.description: Lines it is about, each `repo:path:from-to`, quoted from the checkout's files as they are now.

note.description: Append a note signed by the calling worker, the text form of `append`: it quotes each anchor's lines from the checkout's files itself.

to.description: The worker's callsign, looked for on the caller's floor, then on every floor.

send.description: Submit into a worker a pointer to the notes on its checkout's thread new to it, sent by the calling worker.

of.description: The callsign of the worker whose work is reviewed, looked for on the caller's floor, then on every floor: the reviewer starts on that worker's.

tell.description: The reviewer sends a pointer to its notes to the author when done.

review.description: Hire a reviewer as the calling worker, the typed form of `hire`: never limited, and the reply says where it starts.

anchors/<project>.description: Where each anchor of a worker's thread stands among its changes against its default branch, by `<n>|<i>` (its note's number and its place among the note's anchors): `same` where its quote still reads in the diff (or, for an anchor without a quote, while its file has changes), `changed` where the file changed and it doesn't, `gone` where the file has no changes left.

card.description: The worker's id: its thread's anchors, among its changes.

history/<project>.description: The project's review threads, live and landed (filed by Tidy), oldest first, and what each author wrote in them.

said/<project>.description: What a checkout's thread says, read as `reader`: its file's text, the notes new to the reader, the lines printed after the text (or in its place while it has none), and with `sender`, the prompt Send types into the reader.

reader.description: Whose view: a callsign, or the user's name.

sender.description: Who sends the notes to the reader: a callsign, or `the user`.

hirer.description: The callsign of the worker that hired the reader: Send tells it to report there.

thread/<project>.description: A checkout's thread as the caller reads it: its file, the notes new to the caller, and how its anchors are named. No checkout named, the caller's: a reviewer's is its author's.
